blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What actually happens in a session

rows: A short conversation or form to name the actual decision on the table - a stream choice, a course shortlist, a job offer, a stay-vs-pivot fork - instead of a vague "help me with my career" starting point.
Structured interest, personality, aptitude, or skill signals gathered through tested tools, not a five-minute impression formed from small talk.

A counsellor talks through what the self-assessment shows against real options - courses, roles, entrance exams, hiring patterns - and how they line up with your actual constraints: money, location, family expectations, timeline.
The session closes with a stated direction or shortlist you can act on, not an open-ended summary of the conversation you have to interpret yourself afterward.
A concrete follow-up action - a course to research, an application to start, a skill to begin building, or a further session if the decision needs ongoing support.
